What flood insurance really costs where you live

Answers from FEMA's own policy and claim records: what people near you pay, whether you're required to buy it, and how fast it starts.

Built from 1,572 NFIP policy records and 501 claim records downloaded from FEMA: every record for each state shown, matched to FEMA’s own count. How we check them

Three things to know first

How fast does it start? Buy it now: most policies start 30 days after you buy, but there's no wait if you buy it with a new or refinanced mortgage.

Am I required to buy it? Only if your home is in a high-risk zone (A or V) and your mortgage is from a federally regulated lender, or federal help to buy or build (42 U.S.C. §4012a). Check your zone on FEMA's flood map.

Does my homeowners policy cover floods? Most homeowners insurance does not cover flood damage; flood insurance is bought separately, through the federal NFIP or a private insurer.
